motion.name: ease-sign
motion.purpose: Every hover: 0.16s on signs, chips and Submit, 0.18s on the exit bar, 0.2s on arrows. Stage signs lift 2px, chips press 1px.

motion.name: fold-unfold
motion.value: smoothstep over the fold top at 1.0 to 0.45 of viewport height; rotateX(-58deg to 0) about 50% 0; perspective 1400px at 50% 12%
motion.purpose: The one 3D event. Desktop (1024px and up) with motion allowed and JavaScript on. 58.0 deg at 100%, 47.4 at 85%, 25.1 at 70%, 10.6 at 60%, 0 at 45%.

motion.name: reading-line
motion.purpose: Where the route fill, the odometer and the current stop read.

motion.name: route-fill
motion.purpose: The asphalt road draws down each fold rail, at every width, until reduced motion.

motion.name: odometer
motion.purpose: Counts 60 down to 0 along the strip; the form plate reads "Early access 0 km".

motion.name: country-drift
motion.value: --drift (0 to 1) times a per-layer (dx, dy): clouds 60,-8; far 26,-14; mid 1 -18,-22; mid 2 24,-30; trees -30,-36; rocks -44,-8
motion.purpose: Translation only. The hero drifts with its scroll share, the wide-desktop tour backdrop with the tour. The ground stays.

motion.name: frame-loop
motion.value: one pending requestAnimationFrame; passive scroll listener
motion.purpose: Scroll and resize schedule the update. A media-query change clears the state under reduced motion and re-runs it otherwise.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition and animation 0.01ms; no folding, drift or odometer; route drawn; smooth scroll off
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. No JavaScript behaves the same: --unfold 1, --fill 1, --drift 0.

narrative.overview:
The page is the drive to the holiday. A visitor meets one wide green guide sign over a road that runs into layered ranges, reads the offer in a second, then follows a single route down the page. Six brown tourist signs mark the stops (Plan, Stay, Crew, Care, Fund and claim, Report on time), each opening onto the real product with sample data, until the road ends at the early-access form, marked "Early access 0 km". It is a Persuade surface for operations leads and coordinators at Australian NDIS providers that run supported holidays. The offer has to read as serious software, not as a holiday or transport company, so the sign grammar is restrained, the lettering is plain, the country does the nature work and the real screens do the proving.

The world is Australian road wayfinding with three sign colours and one job each. Green guide signs carry the offer and the destination. White-on-brown tourist signs mark each stop. Blue service signs are used only for Sign in. White Overpass lettering inside a white ring inset from the panel's edge is the whole sign language. The country the road runs through is authored SVG (Pale Slate sky, fern and olive ranges, Pale Sprout paddocks, ochre sandstone, white-trunked gums) and never carries copy.

The page is spacious, signed and staged; the app is dense and tonal, with shadows only on what acts or floats. They share only values copied by hand: the Organic Ledger greens, ink and paper, Manrope for reading and Material Symbols for pictograms. This file owns the landing's tokens, type roles, components and motion. Nothing here is imported into the app, and nothing from the app is imported here.

The page carries its own direction contract: a comment above the doctype in `index.html`, 150 words or fewer, in six labelled blocks (THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM, FINISH) that name the form ("Australian road wayfinding", candidate 3 of 7), the seed key 9680af9b and the staging ("folding volume": a concertina-folded road strip map). Its thesis is the rule everything below serves: the page is the drive to the holiday, one route, six exits and a destination, with no gradient hero, laptop mock-up or icon grid. The comment stays first in the file (pinned) and in the built page (a release check); with it there the page still renders in standards mode (checked in a browser in R1).
keyCharacteristics: Three sign colours, one job each: green is the offer, brown is the route and its stops, blue is Sign in
A sign is a coloured panel with a white ring inset from its edge, white Overpass lettering and a ring-bordered pictogram box
One route, six numbered stops counting down 60 km to 10 km, and the form at 0 km
The only 3D is the concertina: each stop is a paper sheet hinged at its top crease that unfolds (rotateX 58 degrees to flat) as it arrives, on desktop with motion allowed
Real product screens at natural size, each captioned with a "Sample data" tag; art-directed crops below 1024px
Authored SVG country; no photographs, no remote images, no icon font
Open by default: with no JavaScript or with reduced motion every fold is flat, the route fully drawn and the country still; under 1024px the folds stay flat and only the route draws
Claims only from the confirmed safe list; every number counted from the code

rules.name: The Sign Colour Rule
rules.body: Green is the offer and the destination, brown is the route and what sits on it, blue is Sign in. A sign colour never changes job. Blue appears on exactly three links today, all to `/login`.

rules.name: The Retroreflective White Rule
rules.body: White is a sign material: lettering, rings, rules, pictogram boxes, disc icons and the fields a visitor types into on a sign. It is also the canvas of a proof frame. It is never a page ground.

rules.name: The Country Stays Behind Rule
rules.body: The scenery is decorative (`aria-hidden`), static under reduced motion and never carries copy. Text sits on signs, paper, sand or a paper-tinted label. The one exception is the tour heading and lede over the wide-desktop backdrop, measured at 9.7:1 or better (R2).

rules.name: The Tinted Ground Rule
rules.body: No colour in the stylesheet is `#000`. Text is Ledger Ink, shadows take the dark of the surface they fall on, and band grounds are only country colours or Warm Paper.

rules.name: The Sign Voice Rule
rules.body: Overpass says, Manrope explains. Names, labels, figures and controls are Overpass; sentences, captions, intros, notes and typed text are Manrope. Headings use `text-wrap: balance`, paragraphs `text-wrap: pretty`.

rules.name: The Two Ranges Rule
rules.body: The only faces are Overpass 600 to 800 and Manrope 400 to 700, requested as two variable ranges from Google Fonts with `display=swap`. Both Latin subsets are preloaded so the hero's lettering is in place before first paint (CLS 0). Adding a face or weight is a new request and a new layout-shift risk.

rules.name: The Text Floor Rule
rules.body: Page text is never below 13px (0.8125rem). Text inside a proof screen is never below 12px as displayed (R1 fix 6, which is why crops exist). Km markers and odometer figures use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Cast-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows fall down and out, long (24px to 60px) with a negative spread, in a tint from the Shadow tints list. Hover lifts at most 2px (stage signs) and presses 1px (chips).

rules.name: The One-3D Rule
rules.body: The fold is the only perspective on the page: one axis (rotateX at the sheet's top crease), 58 degrees at its peak, 1400px perspective, desktop with motion allowed. Everything else is flat and moves by translation only (the country's drift, the arrow nudges).

dos: **Do** give each sign colour one job: green guide signs carry the offer and destination, brown tourist signs mark the route and its stops, blue service signs appear only on Sign in.

**Do** build every sign as a coloured panel with a white ring inset by its variant's gap, white Overpass lettering and a ring-bordered pictogram box, taking radius, gap and stroke from the variant table.
**Do** set anything a sign says (names, labels, figures, controls) in Overpass 600 to 800 and anything read (sentences, captions, intros, typed text) in Manrope 400 to 700.

**Do** keep the route honest: stops numbered 1 to 6 at 60, 50, 40, 30, 20 and 10 km and the form at 0 km. Change a stop's name, order or pictogram in the stops list, the stage sign, the shield, the fold id, the aria ids, the alt text and `page.test.ts` together.

**Do** keep the concertina's numbers (smoothstep, 1.0 to 0.45 of the viewport height, 58 degree peak, 1400px perspective, reading line at 60%) and check any change with a four-frame filmstrip at fold-top 98, 85, 70 and 60% of the viewport; the sentence must stay legible at the reading line.

**Do** make every motion default to open: with no JavaScript or with reduced motion every fold must be flat, the route fully drawn and the country still; under 1024px the folds stay flat whatever the preference.

**Do** show real screens from the real app at natural size, each in a figure whose caption starts with the "Sample data" tag and says only what the screen shows, with alt text that is a full sentence of what is on screen.
**Do** serve an art-directed `-m` crop below 1024px for every wide screen, 1x and 2x WebP, with `width` and `height` equal to the file's size, `loading="lazy"` and `decoding="async"`.

**Do** crop out app defects and fixture-only labels instead of showing them (raw enum text, the dark-on-dark body-map pill, authored notes boxes), and keep the footer's "some on-screen notes were written for the sample".

**Do** state counts exactly as the code counts them (18 roster checks: 2 hard stops, 16 warnings, 4 that ask for a reason; 11 incident types; 5 credentials; 3 funding types; 25 audited record types) and re-count them on the release commit.

**Do** say what Odip is in the first viewport: trip management software for NDIS providers that run supported holidays, one record for travellers, accommodation, staff, vehicles and funding, then the claims.
**Do** name every action for assistive tech at every width: the short header label stays visible and the link carries `aria-label="Request early access"`.
**Do** make a sideways scroll frame a `role="group"` named "Screen: <caption>, scrolls sideways", focusable only while it really scrolls, with the fade and hint only then.
**Do** keep the two-tone 3px focus ring on every interactive element and 44px or more on every target.

**Do** keep the form honest: a neutral collection notice identical under the form and in the footer, `TODO(release)` comments for facts the owner has not supplied (a timeframe is stated only if it will be honoured), a success message that repeats the typed address, typed values kept on every failure, and a duplicate email answered exactly like a new one.
**Do** show errors as text with a glyph on a tinted row, never colour alone, and move focus to the first invalid field or, with none, to the status line.
**Do** ship Submit disabled with the no-JavaScript note visible by default, and let the script hide the note and enable the button.
**Do** keep to the CSP: same-origin scripts only and none inline, images from self, data and blob, fonts from Google Fonts, fetch to self; the art stays authored SVG.
donts: **Don't** build the NDIS SaaS template: the contract's "no gradient hero, laptop mock-up or icon grid", plus stock photography, a logo strip, a testimonial carousel or a pricing table. The sky, grass and sand bands are the country's horizon drawn from the palette, not a gradient hero.
**Don't** invent proof: no customers, testimonials, pricing, press, logos or ratings, and no customer count above one.

**Don't** claim integrations (Xero, Brevity, Employment Hero, Splose, Linxio, Budgetly), connecting or submitting to PRODA or the NDIS Commission, a 5-day rule or live countdown timers, a complaints register, offline mode or a PWA, data residency, e-signing, payment reconciliation, SMS, or per-traveller bed or room allocation. `page.test.ts` pins most of these words.

**Don't** over-read a feature. The 24 hours run from when the incident record was created in Odip, so say "unreported 24 hours after it was logged"; Odip flags it, the form does not; say "keeps an audit history of changes", never "every change". A shift note that mentions an injury "prompts" an incident report (an advisory keyword scan with false positives and negatives), never "flags" or "detects". Roster checks: "Two block the shift; the others warn, and some ask for a reason", never "the rest".
**Don't** promise an outcome in a name: the sixth stop is "Report on time", never "Stay compliant".
**Don't** say "rooms": the product reserves bed and bedroom counts. Say "accommodation".
**Don't** say Odip connects to PRODA: Odip exports the files and the provider uploads them. Say "PRODA bulk file" and re-check the "BPR CSV" and "PRODA file" labels on each release.
**Don't** use hype or scarcity: no exclamation marks, "limited places" or "hurry" (pinned).
**Don't** use blue for anything but Sign in, put copy on the scenery, or use `#000`.

**Don't** front-load the unfold. The easeOutCubic version spent 34 to 15 degrees inside the bottom 15% of the screen and read as a shade-in (R1 fix 4). Do not shorten the 1.0 to 0.45 range or lower the 58 degree peak without a filmstrip.
**Don't** ship a dead control: no `noscript` wrapper for the form note, and the script blocked with JavaScript on must look the same as JavaScript off (R1 fix 9).
**Don't** show a screen too small to read: no thumbnails, no proof text under 12px as shown, no run of nested sideways scrollers hiding the proof (R1 fix 6).
**Don't** let a scroll frame become a landmark: seven identical "region" labels failed axe (R1 fix 1).
**Don't** hide the short Request label from assistive tech (R1 fix 1).
**Don't** let blur validation move the layout under a pressed Submit.
**Don't** import the app's tokens, components or utilities here, or copy these tokens into the app.
**Don't** add a third face, an icon font, a photograph, a remote image, an inline script or a third-party script.
**Don't** add a figure without all of it: lazy 1x and 2x WebP, real alt text, manifest dimensions, the Sample-data tag and a manifest entry that says whether it is fixture-fed.

**Don't** let a fixture show a state the product cannot produce. A fixture-fed screen is flagged `fixture: true`, shows only labels the real API can send, and anything else waits on a recapture from real data (the "NDIA Managed" badge is the open case).
